memories.text: I've been in Valencia since uni, in an old building in Ruzafa, and the summers are brutal.
Right now I code at Huerta Foods, mostly the ordering system, and nobody tests anything.
Professionally I'm a backend developer, APIs and databases mostly, no fancy frontends.
I'm obsessed with padel at the moment, and I play three evenings a week with my cousins.
When you show me code, use Python please, not pseudo-code or JavaScript.
Doctors double-checked last year and I'm not allergic to eggs, so tortilla is safe.
My older sister Carmen lives in Seville with her two kids and a very loud dog.
Our sprint demo is on Wednesdays right after lunch, so nobody pays attention.
My deploy checklist: run the migration dry-run, tag the release, deploy to staging, wait for the smoke tests, then promote to production.
I got assigned to Faro, a project that tracks cargo containers in real time.
Faro is still being scoped, we haven't written a single line of code yet.
I play for the Turia Futsal Club on Sunday mornings, mostly as a goalkeeper.
Spent a weekend in Lisbon eating pastéis de nata and getting lost in Alfama.
Kiwi gives me a really itchy throat, so I'm allergic to kiwi and avoid fruit salads.
For paella I make the sofrito first, add bomba rice, never stir after the stock goes in, and let the socarrat form at the end.
Correction: sprint demos moved to Fridays, so at least people are in a good mood.
My best friend's bachelor party is going to be in Ibiza this September.
Faro is owned by the Bilbao Port Authority, which is why the meetings are so formal.
Faro is paused while a security audit goes through the whole design.
During Las Fallas I watched the nightly fireworks from my roof with the neighbours.
The bachelor party is not in Ibiza anymore, we switched it to Porto because flights were cheaper.
We got a parrot from my uncle and it already shouts hola at six in the morning.
I don't have a car anymore since I sold it, and the bike lanes are good enough.
Remind me to renew my ID card before the 1st of July.
Moved to Bilbao in February, and I still can't believe how green everything is.
Since February I've been working at Cantabria Cloud on their storage platform.
Cantabria Cloud has its headquarters in Santander, an hour and a bit from here.
My manager at Cantabria is Lucía Ferrer, she's the best engineer on the team.
Lucía lives in Madrid and only comes up north for the quarterly offsite.
I registered for the Bilbao night marathon in October, so I'm running every morning now.
I barely play padel anymore; bouldering at the gym down the street is my thing now.
Faro shipped to production last week and the port is already asking for new features.
Just got back from a road trip around Iceland, the waterfalls were ridiculous.
I had to drop out of the night marathon at kilometre 30 with a calf strain.
For my tax return I download the draft from the tax agency, check the deductions line by line, and submit before June.
I've never been to Asia, but Japan is on the list for next year.
I fall asleep to podcasts about Roman history every single night.
Remind me to claim my old rental deposit back before the end of September.
